title: Strict source regions
question: Should Doubt reject evidence that lacks an exact source region?
verdict: Keep exact locators and bounded excerpts as a fail-closed requirement, while describing the guarantee as traceability rather than truth.

nodes.label: Current position
nodes.text: Reject evidence without an exact source region.

nodes.label: Enforced fields
nodes.text: Every source must include valid publication and retrieval dates, a bounded locator, and a substantive excerpt.

nodes.label: Adversarial coverage
nodes.text: Committed mutations verify malformed dates, unbounded locators, and invalid excerpts are rejected.

nodes.label: Guarantee boundary
nodes.text: The public documentation explicitly says structural validation does not establish source truth or faithful AI extraction.

nodes.label: Qualification
nodes.text: A perfectly bounded quotation can still be misleading, outdated, or unrelated to the edge note.

nodes.label: Missing evidence
nodes.text: Doubt does not yet deterministically verify that an excerpt entails the evidence text and reasoning edge.

edges.note: The rule makes every evidence card navigable to a bounded region.
The specific failure modes are covered by reproducible fixtures.
Strict traceability can look stronger than it is if users mistake it for fact checking.
Region quality and inferential fit remain separate from region presence.
An entailment audit would address the most important gap left by structural validation.

sources.title: Doubt map validator
sources.excerpt: Each source must provide valid publication and retrieval dates, a safe URL or local path, a bounded locator, and a 40–500 character excerpt.

sources.title: Evidence-contract adversarial cases
sources.locator: Section: source-date, source-locator, thin-excerpt, oversized-excerpt cases
sources.excerpt: The deterministic suite mutates source dates and locators, replaces an excerpt with Too short, and creates a 501-character excerpt; every invariant must fire.

sources.title: Doubt README
sources.excerpt: This benchmark measures structural traceability and safe rendering. It does not pretend to measure whether a source is true or whether an AI extracted it faithfully.
